newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - July 24.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- SING TAO said the government should draw up a long-term plan to solve the problems of old and dangerous buildings in Hong Kong. It said private developers should be given more power to go ahead with their redevelopment projects, while a series of measures should be made to protect the interests of old property owners.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said whatever Taiwan authorities did -- including changing the constitution and encouraging other countries to advocate Taiwan joining the United Nations -- could not change the fact that the island was part of China. The paper urged Taiwan to consider seriously the concept of "one country, two systems".

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said the free market philosophy had served Hong Kong extremely well through the years and would continue to do so in the future. It said interventionist policies ran counter to everything that had been achieved in Hong Kong. The present simple tax system should not be sacrificed, the paper urged.
